title: A table of budget cuts on one model and one solver

blocks.text: A school district picks which building repairs to fund this summer, with a binary $`x_j`$ per repair, value $`v_j`$, cost $`c_j`$ and one budget row:
\max \sum_j v_j x_j \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_j c_j x_j \le B \;\; \text{(budget)}, \qquad x_j \in \{0, 1\}

The board wants the best value under several cuts of $`B`$: for each share $`s`$ in `cuts`, the optimum with the budget row's limit at $`(1 - s) B`$, where $`B`$ is the limit the row has when the function is called.

Write `cut_table(model, budget_row, cuts)`, which returns a list with the optimal objective value for each share, in order. Use one `mathopt.IncrementalSolver` on HiGHS for all of them, and edit the row's `upper_bound` rather than building anything new. When the function returns, the model must be exactly as it was, limit included. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def cut_table(model: mathopt.Model, budget_row, cuts: list[float]) -> list[float]:
    """The optimum for each relative cut of the budget row's current limit; the model is left as it was."""
    original = budget_row.upper_bound
    values = []
    with mathopt.IncrementalSolver(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS) as solver:
        try:
            for share in cuts:
                budget_row.upper_bound = (1 - share) * original
                values.append(solver.solve().objective_value())
        finally:
            budget_row.upper_bound = original
    return values


def build(repairs: dict[str, tuple[float, float]], budget: float):
    """repairs: name -> (value, cost)."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="repairs")
    x = {r: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{r}") for r in repairs}
    row = model.add_linear_constraint(sum(repairs[r][1] * x[r] for r in repairs) <= budget, name="budget")
    model.maximize(sum(repairs[r][0] * x[r] for r in repairs))
    return model, x, row


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, x, row = build({"roof": (9, 6), "boiler": (7, 5), "windows": (4, 3)}, 10)
    print(cut_table(model, row, [0.0, 0.2]))

from cuts import build, cut_table

repairs = {"heating": (80, 55), "lift": (65, 40), "toilets": (35, 20), "paint": (20, 15), "fence": (15, 10)}
model, x, row = build(repairs, 120)

shares = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5]

cases.says: a single cut gives the optimum a fresh solve of the cut model gives, and a cut of 0 gives the base optimum
after the table the model has the same rows and variables as before
a 10% cut after a 20% cut is answered as a 10% cut of the original limit
after the table the row's upper bound is its original value

concepts: several cuts of one limit answered with one incremental solver on one model
